title: Mobility exposure varies sharply by household income and race in 2024 ACS PUMS
source_unit: 2024 ACS 1-year PUMS housing and person records joined by SERIALNO

observations.method: PUMS housing records grouped by HINCP and weighted by WGTP; VEH=0 defines no vehicle. Income bands are under $35k, $35k-$74k, and $75k or more.
observations.uncertainty: PUMS sampling and nonsampling error apply; no replicate-weight interval is calculated in this first layer. HINCP is past-year household income, not liquid cash or transport affordability.
observations.counterinterpretation: No vehicle does not establish unmet work, care, food, or medical access; transit, walking, rideshare, and social networks may substitute.

observations.method: Same PUMS housing method as the low-income observation.
observations.uncertainty: PUMS sampling and nonsampling error apply; no replicate-weight interval is calculated. Higher past-year income does not measure current liquidity, housing location, or schedule control.
observations.subgroup: US households with HINCP $75,000 or more.
observations.counterinterpretation: Greater vehicle availability does not remove long commutes, fuel and repair costs, or geographic distance.

denominator.unit: PWGTP-weighted workers with positive JWMNP commute minutes

observations.method: PUMS person records joined to valid-income households by SERIALNO; JWMNP>=30 defines a 30-plus-minute commute and positive JWMNP excludes work-from-home records.
observations.uncertainty: No replicate-weight interval is calculated. The positive-commute universe excludes people working from home and the cross-section does not observe fare, reliability, care purpose, or missed activity.
observations.subgroup: Workers age 16+ in households with HINCP under $35,000.
observations.counterinterpretation: A lower long-commute share can reflect nonemployment, work-from-home selection, shorter local jobs, or unobserved non-work travel rather than easier total mobility.

observations.period: 2024; workers age 16+ with HINCP $75k or more

denominator.unit: PWGTP-weighted workers with positive JWMNP commute minutes

observations.method: Same PUMS person-household join and commute universe as the low-income observation.
observations.uncertainty: No replicate-weight interval is calculated. Commute duration is not total time burden or proof of chosen versus constrained travel.
observations.subgroup: Workers age 16+ in households with HINCP $75,000 or more.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher-income workers may have longer commutes because of job and housing sorting while retaining more monetary and schedule alternatives; those alternatives are not measured here.

observations.period: 2024; Black workers age 16+ with positive commute minutes

denominator.unit: PWGTP-weighted workers with RAC1P=2 and positive JWMNP

observations.method: Same PUMS commute universe; race uses official 2024 PUMS RAC1P code list.
observations.uncertainty: No replicate-weight interval is calculated; race is a classification, not a mechanism, and household income, occupation, place, and transit quality are not jointly adjusted.
observations.subgroup: Workers coded Black or African American alone.
observations.counterinterpretation: The descriptive difference from White workers does not identify discrimination, geography, occupation, or unequal access as the cause.

observations.period: 2024; White workers age 16+ with positive commute minutes

denominator.unit: PWGTP-weighted workers with RAC1P=1 and positive JWMNP

observations.method: Same PUMS commute universe; race uses official 2024 PUMS RAC1P code list.
observations.uncertainty: No replicate-weight interval is calculated; this is an unadjusted cross-sectional subgroup comparison.
observations.counterinterpretation: The lower share does not establish lower total mobility burden because distance, vehicle costs, care travel, and non-work travel are not measured here.

boundary: This is a descriptive 2024 PUMS cross-sectional layer. Housing measures use WGTP and person commute measures use PWGTP after a SERIALNO join. The income gradient is household past-year income; the commute universe excludes work-from-home records. The layer does not establish transport affordability, reliability, care access, missed activity, discrimination, or political/cultural response. The official 2024 PUMS data dictionary was used to correct RAC1P coding before promotion.
